bug_description: The Draco OBJ decoder accepts OBJ face definitions whose texture-coordinate or normal indices refer to entries that were never declared in the file. The parser validates only that each index is non-zero; it never checks that the index fits within the number of vt / vn / v entries seen in the first parsing pass. The unchecked index is stored directly into the per-point attribute mapping (indices_map_) and later dereferenced by the attribute deduplication stage, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read in PointAttribute::DeduplicateFormattedValues. The vulnerability is reachable from the public ObjDecoder::DecodeFromBuffer API and from the shipped draco_encoder / draco_decoder command-line tools when given an attacker-controlled .obj file.
build_sh:
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -eu
cd /src/draco

# Build draco as a static library using cmake
mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$CC" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$CXX" \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$CXXFLAGS" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DDRACO_BUILD_EXECUTABLES=OFF
make -j$(nproc)

# Compile harness against the static library
cd /src
$CXX $CXXFLAGS \
    -std=c++17 \
    -I /src/draco/src \
    -I /src/draco/build \
    /src/harness.cc \
    /src/draco/build/libdraco.a \
    -lpthread \
    -o /src/harness_bin
secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR draco.issue-1194..."
    /src/harness_bin /testcase/poc.obj
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/draco
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"
    case "$command" in
        build) build "$@" ;;
        repro) repro "$@" ;;
        patch) patch "$@" ;;
        *) echo "Unknown command: $command"; echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi
dockerfile:
FROM hwiwonlee/secb.base:latest
ENV FUZZING_LANGUAGE=c++
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y git cmake
RUN git clone https://github.com/google/draco.git draco \
    && cd draco \
    && git checkout 77e616e \
    && rm -rf .git \
    && git init \
    && git config user.email "secbench@local" \
    && git config user.name "secbench" \
    && git add -A && git commit -m "draco at 77e616e (pre-patch)"
WORKDIR $SRC/draco
COPY harness.cc $SRC/harness.cc
COPY build.sh $SRC/
RUN mkdir -p /testcase
COPY poc.obj /testcase/poc.obj

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/google/draco/issues/1194
## Description:
Issue: google/draco#1194
Title: Out-of-bounds read in draco::PointAttribute::DeduplicateFormattedValues
State: open
Created at: 2026-05-06

Issue Body:
The Draco OBJ decoder accepts OBJ face definitions whose texture-coordinate or normal indices refer to entries that were never declared in the file. The parser validates only that each index is non-zero; it never checks that the index fits within the number of vt / vn / v entries seen in the first parsing pass. The unchecked index is stored directly into the per-point attribute mapping (indices_map_) and later dereferenced by the attribute deduplication stage, producing an out-of-bounds read in PointAttribute::DeduplicateFormattedValues.

The vulnerability is reachable from the public ObjDecoder::DecodeFromBuffer API and from the shipped draco_encoder / draco_decoder command-line tools when given an attacker-controlled .obj file.

Affected component:
- Version: 1.5.7 (current main, commit 77e616e)
- File: src/draco/io/obj_decoder.cc
- Entry points: draco::ObjDecoder::DecodeFromBuffer(DecoderBuffer*, PointCloud*), draco::ObjDecoder::DecodeFromBuffer(DecoderBuffer*, Mesh*)
